name: TCRT5000 IR line tracking sensor
description: Reflective infrared line / surface sensor: a Vishay TCRT5000 (950 nm IR LED plus phototransistor, best at about 2.5 mm, works 0.2-15 mm) on a small LM393 comparator board. AO is the phototransistor collector (10 kOhm pull-up to VCC): near VCC over black or nothing, falling towards 0 V over a white surface. DO (open collector, 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC) goes LOW when AO falls below the trimmer threshold, i.e. over a white/reflective surface, and HIGH over a black line. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: TCRT5000 IR line tracking sensor module (common blue 4-pin LM393 clone board: VCC, GND, DO, AO).
eli5: Shines invisible light at the floor and tells your board whether it is looking at a white surface or a black line, so a robot can follow a track.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (pin 1). On an ESP32 or Pico use 3V3: DO and AO are pulled up to VCC.

pins.name: DO
pins.description: Digital output (pin 3), LM393 open collector with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC: LOW over a white/reflective surface (indicator LED on), HIGH over a black line or nothing.

pins.name: AO
pins.description: Analog output (pin 4): phototransistor collector, about VCC with no reflection, lower the more IR is reflected. Optional.

supplierQuery: TCRT5000 IR line tracking sensor module LM393 4 pin
buildNotes: Header order as printed: VCC, GND, DO, AO. Some newer boards print VCC, DO, AO, GND instead; check the silkscreen before wiring.
On an ESP32 or Pico power VCC from 3V3: DO and AO are pulled up to VCC through 10 kOhm, so a 5 V supply puts 5 V on the GPIO.
DO is LOW over white (the green switch LED lights) and HIGH over a black line or when nothing is within range.
Mount the sensor about 2-10 mm above the floor; the TCRT5000 peaks at 2.5 mm and fades beyond about 15 mm.
Turn the trimmer until the switch LED is on over the white surface and off over the black line.
AO is optional: read it with an ADC for a graded reflection value (lower = more reflection). Sunlight contains IR and can upset it.

sim.quantity: White / reflective surface under sensor (DO low)

example.code:
from tcrt5000 import TCRT5000
import time

sensor = TCRT5000({DO})
while True:
    print('Surface: %s' % ('white' if sensor.reflective() else 'black'))
    time.sleep(0.5)

test.title: Reports a white surface when the sensor sees reflection

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading. Not yet tested on real hardware.
